episode_title: HPH403: From landlord to high-performance developer – with David Bradley-Bowles

real_qa.q: What costs between £1,600 and £2,000 per square metre to build at scale compared to traditional construction?
real_qa.r: You can build a passive house at scale between £1,600 per square metre and £2,000 per square metre, which is actually not that much more expensive than a traditional build. This is reasonably achievable and the build costs are not through the roof, though maintaining program speed and consistency without rework is critical to profitability.
real_qa.requete: passive house cost per square metre

real_qa.q: Why did David Bradley-Bowles transition from being a landlord to building passive houses?
real_qa.r: He got tired of dealing with problems that came out of the woodwork with old homes. He started looking at the blueprint side of things to build first-time good quality stock that would last for the duration of the business, working with investors to fund developments that provided a smoother, slicker system that wasn't just ongoing maintenance all the time. This led him into construction and eventually passive house, which he saw as the right direction for building a robust business suitable for 2030.
real_qa.requete: David Bradley-Bowles landlord to passive house developer

real_qa.q: What happened to Pure Spring Meadows construction company in 2025?
real_qa.r: At the end of 2025, the construction company went into administration. This was linked to the costs of delivering schemes, but was compounded by the fact that the housing market was slow and last year was a quiet year for sales.

real_qa.q: What percentage of new build housing in the UK is produced by the five major house builders versus SMEs?
real_qa.r: In the UK, 80% of new build housing is done by the five major house builders while only 20% is done by SMEs. This contrasts sharply with Germany, where the market is predominantly 80% made up of SME builders and only 20% made up by big corporates, giving SMEs in Germany much more scope to drive quality metrics in the market.
real_qa.requete: UK house building market share major developers SME percentage

real_qa.q: How did construction costs change between 2019 and 2025 for building projects?
real_qa.r: The price of construction in 2019 was 40% down on where it was in 2025, representing a ridiculous rise in costs over six to seven years. This increase was compounded by interest rates going up in 2023, further increases in materials and labour, and scarce land supply with landowners sitting on land rather than selling at market value.

guest.bio_context: David Bradley-Bowles began his career as a landlord working on old Victorian homes and renovations from 2004 to 2015, before transitioning into construction and passive house development. Frustrated with ongoing maintenance issues in traditional housing stock, he shifted his focus to designing and building high-performance homes from scratch. He has progressed from building two proof-of-concept passive houses in South Bradford with BT Passive certification, to scaling up to 20-home schemes and affordable housing projects with community groups, while simultaneously developing expertise across architecture, engineering, site delivery, and sustainable construction practices.

real_quote: Scaling a passive house is reasonably achievable. The build costs are not through the roof, but you still need to be able to run a program quickly, consistently, without interruptions, without rework, without pulling people back in.
key_stats: 2004 to 2015: period when David Bradley-Bowles worked predominantly on old housing stock as landlord, letting agent, and renovation specialist
2 homes: initial proof-of-concept passive house project built in South Bradford, valued at less than half a million pounds
20 homes: larger scheme scaling to over one million pounds in value
£1,600 to £2,000 per square metre: cost range for building passive houses at scale
£3,000+ per square metre: typical cost for self-builds in the UK
2019 to 2025: construction costs increased by approximately 67% (40% lower in 2019 than in 2025)
80% major developers vs 20% SMEs: distribution of UK new build housing market
80% SMEs vs 20% major corporates: distribution of German building market
2023: year when interest rates increased significantly, raising the cost of lending
2025: the year Pure Spring Meadows construction company went into administration following market slowdown
